confidence_notes: Hampi is a small heritage village with no Numbeo-style city index, so the food and drink anchors are bounded estimates. I ran four web searches: one for the RBA rate and three for prices. The RBA search gave a USD/AUD rate of 0.6720 for 2026-11-18, from the RBA exchange-rate pages. The price searches found only traveller-guide figures: a Tripbase-style budget page (coffee about $1, beer about $2, cocktail about $4, budget meal about $1.5, mid-range meal about $5). They also found a blogger's report of beer at about INR 180 in guesthouses, a cheap-restaurant figure of about INR 150 per person, and INR 300-900 for two at Hampi Bazaar restaurants. Most of these sources are undated or old, so I adjusted upward modestly for inflation. I found no Hampi cappuccino price, so the coffee figure rests on generic coffee prices. For Bangalore bars I found draft beer up to about INR 165, wine from about INR 80 for a small glass, and craft cocktails at INR 500-700. Hampi bars are far cheaper, and alcohol is only served in some venues, mostly across the river. I set cocktail and wine from the local price relationship to beer (cocktail about 2x beer, wine glass about 1.6x beer). Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge and a hostel-listing snippet showing dorms around $4 and private rooms around $20; I did not search accommodation prices or inspect listings. The 3-star figure is the least certain because Hampi has very few formally rated 3-star hotels, so it is anchored on nearby Hospet and Kamalapura properties. I assumed about INR 88-90 per USD for the conversions, and July is low season.
comparable_city_reasoning: Rural and small-town Karnataka tourist hubs, with a backpacker-oriented village economy similar to Gokarna or Pushkar. Prices are anchored on Hampi guest-house and restaurant reports and adjusted using Karnataka and Bangalore price relationships for drinks.
